title: Just Did, Doing Now & About To
description: 〜たばかり, 〜たところ, 〜ているところ and 〜るところ: the moments before, during and after an action.

points.title: 〜たばかり: have just done (feels recent)
points.summary: た-form + ばかり = 'just did'. It's subjective: it can be minutes or months ago if it feels recent. It can modify nouns: 買ったばかりのパソコン.
points.body:
**た-form + ばかり** means the action happened **only a short time ago**, from the speaker's point of view:
- さっき食べ**たばかり**です (I only just ate).
- 3か月前に日本に来**たばかり**なので、まだ日本語が下手です. Three months can still be 'just'.

**Grammar:**
- It ends with だ/です or なので: 来たばかりだ.
- It modifies nouns with の: 買っ**たばかりの**パソコン (a computer I just bought).

**ばかり vs ところ:**
- **たばかり** is subjective ('it feels recent'), and the time can be long.
- **たところ** is objective: the moment *right after*, typically minutes. It can't modify nouns like this.

Don't confuse it with **noun + ばかり** = 'nothing but' (ゲームばかり).
examples: さっき{食|た}べたばかりだから、おなかがいっぱいです。
I just ate, so I'm full.
{三|さん}か{月前|げつまえ}に{来|き}たばかりなので、まだ{日本語|にほんご}が{下手|へた}です。
I only came three months ago, so my Japanese is still poor.
{買|か}ったばかりのパソコンが{壊|こわ}れました。
The computer I just bought broke.

points.title: 〜たところ: have just (this moment) done
points.summary: た-form + ところだ = the action finished just now. It's the moment right after.
points.body:
**ところ** literally means 'place', and here it marks a **point in time** relative to an action. **た-form + ところ** = 'just finished, right now':
- ちょうど仕事が終わっ**たところ**です (I've just this moment finished work).
- 今起き**たところ**です (I just woke up).

It's often paired with **今** or **ちょうど**.

It can't be used for something a long time ago (三か月前に来たところ ✗). Use たばかり there.

**The ところ family:**
- 〜る**ところ**: about to do
- 〜ている**ところ**: in the middle of doing
- 〜た**ところ**: just finished doing
examples: ちょうど{仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わったところです。
I've just finished work.
{今|いま}、{駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたところです。
I've just arrived at the station.

points.title: 〜ているところ: in the middle of doing
points.summary: て-form + いるところだ = right in the middle of an action. It stresses that the action is in progress at this very moment.
points.body:
**ている + ところ** zooms in on **the middle** of an action: '(right now) I'm in the process of …':
- 今、晩ご飯を作っ**ているところ**です (I'm in the middle of cooking dinner).

**ているところ vs ている:** ている can also mean a habit or state. ているところ is only 'in progress right now', and is often used to explain why you can't do something else: 今、電話している**ところ**だから、あとで.

**Past form:** 〜ている**ところでした**: I was in the middle of … (when something happened).
examples: {今|いま}、{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{作|つく}っているところです。
I'm in the middle of making dinner.
{今|いま}、{考|かんが}えているところです。もう{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
I'm thinking about it right now. Please wait a little longer.

points.title: 〜るところ: about to do
points.summary: Dictionary form + ところだ = 'just about to do'. The past ところでした means 'was just about to (when …)'.
points.body:
**Dictionary form + ところ** marks the moment **right before** an action:
- これから出かける**ところ**です (I'm just about to go out).
- 今から寝る**ところ**だったのに、電話が来た (I was just about to go to bed when the phone rang).

It's often with **これから** or **今から**.

**Past:** 〜る**ところでした** = 'was about to'. This is common for 'just in time' stories and near-misses: 電話する**ところでした** (I was just about to call you).

Memory trick: the verb tense before ところ tells you where you are in the action:
- **る** (not yet) → **ている** (during) → **た** (just finished).
examples: これから{出|で}かけるところです。
I'm just about to go out.
ちょうど{電話|でんわ}するところでした。
I was just about to call you.
{今|いま}から{寝|ね}るところだったのに、{友達|ともだち}から{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た。
I was just about to go to bed when a friend called.

questions.prompt: {三|さん}か{月前|げつまえ}に{日本|にほん}に{来|き}た（　）なので、まだ{日本語|にほんご}が{下手|へた}です。
questions.explanation: 'Only just came' even three months ago: subjective **たばかり**.
notes: 来たまま means 'still in the state of having come', which doesn't fit.
たところ only covers the moment right after. Three months ago is too long.
来たあいだ isn't grammatical. 間 needs a continuing state.
questions.translation: I only came to Japan three months ago, so my Japanese is still poor.

questions.prompt: さっき{食|た}べた（　）だから、おなかがいっぱいです。
notes: 食べたまま means 'having eaten (and staying that way)', and it doesn't explain being full.
ながら attaches to the ます-stem (食べながら).
食べたあいだ isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: I just ate, so I'm full.

questions.prompt: {買|か}った（　）のパソコンが、もう{壊|こわ}れました。
questions.explanation: **たばかりの + noun**: 'the … I just bought'.
notes: ほど ('extent') doesn't fit.
買ったままのパソコン would mean 'left as bought (e.g. still in the box)'.
たところ can't modify a noun with の like this.
questions.translation: The computer I just bought has already broken.

questions.prompt: A：もしもし、{今|いま}{話|はな}せる？　B：うん、ちょうど{仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わった（　）だよ。
questions.explanation: 'Just this moment finished': た-form + **ところ**.
notes: 終わったあいだ isn't grammatical.
終わったためだ means 'it's because work ended', which doesn't answer the question.
終わったままだ ('remains finished') isn't natural here.
questions.translation: A: Hello, can you talk now? B: Yeah, I've just finished work.

questions.prompt: {今|いま}、{駅|えき}に（　）ところです。これから{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}ります。
questions.explanation: Just arrived, and next comes the train: **た-form + ところ**.
notes: 着くところ = 'about to arrive', but then you couldn't board the train next.
The て-form doesn't go directly before ところ.
The ます-stem can't come before ところ.
questions.translation: I've just arrived at the station. Now I'll get on the train.

questions.prompt: {今|いま}、{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{作|つく}っている（　）です。
questions.explanation: In the middle of doing: **ているところ**.
notes: 作っているまでです isn't grammatical here.
ているばかり means 'doing nothing but…'. It doesn't express 'right now'.
作っているまま isn't natural.
questions.translation: I'm in the middle of making dinner.

questions.prompt: Which means 'I'm **in the middle of** eating'?
questions.explanation: ている + ところ = **during** the action.
notes: 食べるところ = 'about to eat'.
食べたところ = 'just finished eating'.
食べたばかり = 'just ate (recently)'.

questions.prompt: {今|いま}、{考|かんが}えて（　）ところです。もう{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
questions.explanation: 'I'm thinking about it right now': 考えて**いる**ところ.
notes: 考えていないところ isn't a pattern.
考えていたところ = 'was (just) thinking about it', which doesn't fit 'please wait'.
The て-form can't come before ところ.
questions.translation: I'm thinking about it right now. Please wait a bit longer.

questions.prompt: これから{出|で}かける（　）です。
notes: ばかり in the 'just did' sense follows the た-form.
出かけるあいだです isn't grammatical.
出かけるまま isn't natural.
questions.translation: I'm just about to go out.

questions.prompt: Which means 'I was just **about to** call you'?
options: ちょうど{電話|でんわ}したところでした。
ちょうど{電話|でんわ}するところでした。
ちょうど{電話|でんわ}したばかりでした。
ちょうど{電話|でんわ}しているところでした。
questions.explanation: Dictionary form + ところ**でした** = 'was just about to'.
notes: したところ = 'had just called'.
したばかり = 'had only just called'.
しているところ = 'was in the middle of calling'.

questions.prompt: {今|いま}から（　）ところだったのに、{友達|ともだち}から{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た。
questions.explanation: 今から + **dictionary form** + ところだった = 'was about to'.
notes: 寝たところ ('had just gone to bed') clashes with 今から.
寝ないところ isn't a pattern.
The て-form can't come before ところ.
questions.translation: I was just about to go to bed when a friend called.
